fit: 2024 DLB tissue comparison and a measured nutrient in dried figs
assessment: The original measures pantothenic acid in 20 dementia with Lewy bodies and 19 control donors, with lower concentrations in six of ten regions, including primary visual cortex. It mentions visual hallucinations as a possible interpretation of the anatomy. Food composition separately confirms that dried figs contain this nutrient. The tissue comparison has no individual food intake, supplementation, or clinical episode counts.

fit: Parkinson psychosis imaging synthesis across broad symptom definitions
assessment: The published review reports 29 articles and 1,367 participants, of whom 514 had psychosis and 853 did not. It shares PROSPERO CRD42020221904 with the 2022 preprint. Imaging comparisons include heterogeneous hallucination and delusion definitions and no dried fig ingestion outcome.

fit: Parkinson visual symptoms, PET and questionnaires within a specific meeting member
assessment: The ePresentation compares 11 Parkinson patients with visual symptoms and nine without using FDG PET and perceptual or clinical ratings. Relative hypermetabolism and a questionnaire association without multiple-comparison correction have no food exposure or visual episode-rate estimate.

fit: resting EEG microstate transition in Parkinson hallucination phenotype
assessment: The poster compares 19 patients with hallucinations and 20 matched patients. Some transition probabilities differ and duration, occurrence and coverage are broadly similar. Microstate occurrence is an EEG outcome, without a dried fig comparison.

fit: evoked visual EEG in Parkinson minor hallucination phenotype
assessment: The separate poster compares 23 Parkinson patients with minor hallucinations and 23 without. Early visual categorization and later processing responses belong to a stimulus task. The participants' food exposure and spontaneous visual episode frequency are not measured.

fit: Parkinson dementia patient and care partner agreement on psychosis ratings
assessment: The study compares Parkinson dementia patient and caregiver ratings in 21 dyads. Agreement for the SAPS-PD summary score is ICC 0.464, with poor agreement on six of nine items. The source is directly relevant to whose report a symptom scale captures, but neither reporter supplies a food-timed dried fig comparison.

fit: drug-trial NPI-2 composite combines hallucinations and fluctuation
assessment: The meta-analysis uses data from three double-blind randomized donepezil comparisons in dementia with Lewy bodies. The NPI-2 combines hallucinations and cognitive fluctuations. This drug outcome is broader than visual episode frequency and contains no dried fig comparison.

fit: self-reported and measured visual impairment within a dementia cohort
assessment: The analysis covers 624 participants with dementia and distinguishes reported visual impairment from measured near acuity. Neuropsychiatric outcomes are questionnaire measures and not meal-linked observations. There is no dried fig exposure or Parkinson-specific treatment effect in this analysis.

fit: postmortem Parkinson disease dementia tissue marker and measured dried fig constituent
assessment: The study analyzes nine brain regions from nine neuropathologically confirmed Parkinson disease dementia donors and nine controls. Table 2 reports about 40% lower pantothenic acid in case cerebellum, substantia nigra and medulla. Primary visual cortex does not show a clear case–control difference. The comparison measures tissue concentration without dried fig intake or recurrent visual hallucination counts.

fit: cardiac scintigraphy diagnostic classification and visual hallucination features
assessment: The prospective study compares cardiac MIBG in 95 people with mild cognitive impairment. Scans are abnormal in 22 of 37 probable and two of 15 possible Lewy body cases, and normal in 38 of 43 Alzheimer-type cases. The group sizes and probable-Lewy and Alzheimer-type scan counts match EANM 2020 abstract OP-592, marking a single diagnostic cohort. Visual hallucinations are a diagnostic feature. Food intake and episode-rate change are not measured.

fit: analytical composition of the named food preparation
assessment: The authoritative food-composition record FDC 174665 (NDB 09094) identifies dried uncooked figs. The pantothenic acid result is 0.434 mg per 100 g, with eight analytical data points and a reported range of 0.350–0.531 mg per 100 g. This establishes that the ordinary dried fruit contains the nutrient under study. It provides no clinical exposure assessment, brain-tissue response or visual hallucination outcome.
